## Animato v1.7.1 — Animated List Reliability

Animato v1.7.1 is a focused patch release for the Leptos `AnimatedFor`
component. It resolves issues #47, #48, #49, and #50 while preserving the
stable v1 API and the renderer-agnostic core introduced in earlier releases.

### Highlights

- Initial list rows now execute the configured enter animation.
- New `move_delay` support lets existing rows wait before FLIP movement begins.
- The hardcoded 10px list gap has been removed; use the new `gap` prop for
  explicit spacing.
- New `item_class` support exposes generated row wrappers for stacking-context,
  hover z-index, and application-specific styling.
- Entering rows honor `PresenceAnimation` duration and easing, independently
  from move duration and easing.
- Regression tests cover enter timing and delayed movement behavior.
- Leptos docs, examples, architecture, roadmap, changelog, version tests, and
  release automation have been updated for the patch.

### Leptos example

```rust,ignore
<AnimatedFor
    each=items.into()
    key=|item: &Item| item.id
    children=|item: Item| view! { <article>{item.label}</article> }
    enter=PresenceAnimation::slide_up()
    move_duration=0.35
    move_easing=Easing::EaseOutCubic
    move_delay=0.20
    stagger_delay=0.04
    gap=12.0
    item_class="relative z-0 hover:z-50"
/>
```

### Compatibility

No Rust API was removed. `AnimatedFor` no longer inserts an implicit 10px gap.
Applications that intentionally relied on that spacing can retain it with
`gap=10.0`.

### Install

```toml
[dependencies]
animato = "1.7.1"
```

```toml
[dependencies]
animato = { version = "1.7.1", features = ["leptos-csr"] }
leptos = { version = "0.8.19", features = ["csr"] }
```

```sh
npm install @aarambhdevhub/animato-core
```

### Release verification

The publish workflow enforces:

- formatting and clippy with warnings denied,
- full workspace and no-default-features test suites,
- Rust documentation with warnings denied,
- WASM compilation for framework integrations,
- Leptos, Dioxus, and Yew example compilation,
- JavaScript/WASM browser tests and package-size validation,
- coverage, fuzz, benchmark compilation, and crate publish dry-runs.
